title: Anti-Comintern Pact
summary: Germany and Japan concluded an agreement at Berlin on 25 November 1936, ostensibly against the Communist International but implicitly aimed at the Soviet Union. Italy joined by protocol on 6 November 1937. Japan later renounced it in 1939 and acceded to the Tripartite Pact in 1940.

where.modern_name: Berlin, Germany (proxy pin: Berlin, the location Wikidata lists)

importance.justification: Diplomatic alignment of Germany, Japan and Italy that foreshadowed the Axis alliance.

sources.title: Anti-Comintern Pact | Axis Powers, Nazi Germany, Japan | Britannica
